rule: Exposure to one counterparty or group of connected counterparties is a "large exposure" if it is ≥ 10% of the bank's Tier 1 capital. Banks must report all exposures ≥ 10% of Tier 1 (both after and before credit risk mitigation), and all exempted exposures ≥ 10% of Tier 1.
citation: CBUAE Large Exposures Regulation C 1/2023, Art. 2.1, Art. 5.1-5.3 (in force from 26/7/2023)

rule: Total exposure to a single counterparty or group of connected counterparties must not exceed 25% of Tier 1 capital at all times.
Breach must be reported to CBUAE immediately and rectified quickly; Tier 1 capital is reduced by the amount of the breach.
Banks must test for economic interdependence (to build connected groups) in all cases where exposure to one counterparty exceeds 5% of Tier 1. Control is presumed at > 50% voting rights.

Exposures to the UAE Federal Government, the CBUAE, foreign sovereigns rated AA- or better (and their central banks), and 0%-risk-weight MDBs are exempt from the limit, but must still be reported if ≥ 10% of Tier 1.

Aggregate cap 150% of Tier 1 for all Emirate governments combined, including their non-commercial public-sector entities. Direct exposure to an Emirate government has no individual cap; each non-commercial entity is capped at 25% of Tier 1. CBUAE may raise the aggregate cap case by case (with a risk-weight add-on).

Individual cap 25% of Tier 1; aggregate cap 100% of Tier 1. A self-sustaining commercial GRE (profitable, services its own debt) can be treated as separate from its government parent only with CBUAE approval.

Intraday interbank exposures are exempt. All other interbank exposures fall under the general 25% of Tier 1 limit. G-SIB to G-SIB: 15%. UAE banks' aggregate exposure to their own foreign branches: 30% of Tier 1. No grandfathering for interbank (full compliance by 31 Dec 2023).

parameter: Aggregate limit on sum of large exposures
rule: No overall cap on the sum of all large exposures found in C 1/2023 (the Annex 1 summary shows aggregate limits only for government, GRE, related-party and branch categories).

Breaches caused by moving from the old 2013 rules are phased out: grandfathered amount 100% → 75% (31 Dec 2023) → 50% (31 Dec 2024) → 25% (31 Dec 2025) → 0% from 31 Dec 2026. The scheme ends on 31 Dec 2026.
Large exposure limit = lower of 250% of Branch Capital and 25% of entity-level Tier 1. Exposure to head office: max 30% of Branch Capital (funded) and 300% (unfunded).
Shareholders owning ≥ 5% of the bank's capital (with their connected group and related parties): individual 20%, aggregate 50% of Tier 1.

parameter: Related parties: non-bank subsidiaries and affiliates
rule: Individual 10%, aggregate 25% of Tier 1.
Individual 5%, aggregate 25% of Tier 1. If a board member forms a connected group with a ≥ 5% shareholder, the lower board-member limits apply to that group.
Lending to the bank's external auditors is prohibited.

The old fixed cap (20% of total deposits, from Union Law 10/1980) no longer applies (removed 2018 per press). Since 30 Dec 2021 CBUAE uses a real-estate exposure framework measured on credit risk-weighted assets; banks with higher RE exposure face closer supervisory review. No published numeric hard cap found.
citation: The National, 20 Dec 2021; Gulf News, Dec 2021; The National 2018 (see Part C, D)

rule: CBUAE Credit Risk Management Regulation C 3/2024 and Standards C 3/2024 STA, in force from 30/11/2024. Standards are mandatory and enforceable like the regulation.
citation: CBUAE rulebook, C 3/2024 and C 3/2024 STA

rule: Board must approve and regularly review the credit risk strategy, significant policies, limits; and the classification, provisioning, problem-loan and write-off policies.
Board must ensure a delegation matrix for approving facilities; facilities that are material, particularly risky or outside core business must be approved by the Board.

CRO must review in advance all material applications and renewals. Minimum: all facilities needing Senior Management credit committee approval or above. For higher-risk facilities (at least all non-investment grade), the CRO review threshold is 20% below the committee's delegated authority (e.g. AED 100m authority → AED 80m threshold). Wholesale: at obligor level.

parameter: Chief Credit Officer + credit review function
rule: Each bank must have a CCO supported by a credit review function, which reviews all credit proposals. CCO must review obligors every year (wholesale at obligor level), including an updated risk rating based on recent financials, at least annually.

Banks must review performance of individual wholesale facilities at least annually; ratings of all facilities and obligors reviewed at least yearly; internal ratings updated at least every 12 months (more often after credit events).
Classification must be based on internal risk ratings; banks must develop and use internal rating systems; must limit reliance on external ratings and form their own view.

A single master rating scale used across credit management, provisioning and capital. Number of grades must balance accuracy and usability; obligors should spread across most grades; scale must allow robust PD per grade; more granularity in non-investment-grade part. No minimum number of grades is prescribed. Wholesale models must use financial and qualitative factors; overrides limited by notches and count; business-line ratings independently signed off by credit.

> 90 days past due on a material obligation (material = > 5% of the obligor's total funded exposure), or unlikely to pay. Overdraft in excess for > 90 continuous days, or (wholesale) > 90 days in total in any 6 months. Wholesale default is at obligor level (cross-default).

Three stages. SICR (Stage 2) required at > 30 days past due (rebuttable with documented evidence), and for wholesale facilities with ≥ 3 deferrals in a rolling 24 months. Stage 3 sub-buckets for wholesale: 3a (unlikely to pay / 91-180 DPD), 3b (181-365 DPD), 3c (365+ DPD). Rebutting a trigger needs CCO and CRO agreement and top Senior Management committee approval.
Total provisions on Stage 1 and Stage 2 must be ≥ 1.50% of credit risk-weighted assets (CBUAE capital rules). CBUAE may set a higher floor at its discretion.

Unsecured part not covered by expected cash flows: 100%. Unsecured part: ≥ 25% for 4 years from Stage 3, then 100%. Secured part (after haircut): no floor for 4 years, then ≥ 25%. Banks may not use generic statistical LGD for Stage 3 wholesale. 100% provision on unpaid interest/fees > 90 DPD. Provisions booked at least quarterly.

Facility stays in Stage 2 until SICR criteria clear plus a probation of minimum repayments; revolving working-capital lines stay Stage 2 until renewals succeed over at least 12 months. Stage 3 cannot jump straight to Stage 1 for wholesale.
If Stage 3 exposures exceed 5% of total credit exposure, the Board must explain causes to CBUAE and approve a reduction plan, reported semi-annually.
CBUAE Basel III capital regulations effective 1 Feb 2017, with Standards and Guidance (Dec 2022). Standardised approach is the CBUAE credit risk standard; no CBUAE IRB permission regime found.
citation: CBUAE capital adequacy rulebook (see Part D for IRB/output floor)

rule: Exposure to a client or group of connected clients is a "large exposure" when ≥ 10% of the firm's Tier 1 capital. Each large exposure is reported to the PRA; consolidated groups also report exposures ≥ GBP 260m that are below 10% of Tier 1.
citation: PRA Rulebook, Large Exposures (CRR) Part, Arts 392, 394 (versions dated 01/01/2026)

rule: Exposure must not exceed 25% of Tier 1 capital (after credit risk mitigation and exemptions).

Limit is the higher of 25% of Tier 1 or GBP 130m; where GBP 130m applies, it must not exceed 100% of Tier 1 (PRA may allow case by case). G-SII to G-SII: 15% of Tier 1 (comply within 12 months of designation).

Claims on central governments, central banks, PSEs that would get a 0% unsecured risk weight are exempt from the 25% limit. Certain intragroup exposures can be exempt with prior PRA permission. (UK has no GRE-specific regime like the UAE.)

parameter: Aggregate cap on sum of large exposures
rule: None found in the Large Exposures (CRR) Part (only the 100% of Tier 1 ceiling for the GBP 130m interbank case).

No % cap on lending to directors or related parties in PRA rules. Firms must deal with related parties at market value or on terms no more favourable than for unrelated parties; must have policies to identify and control related-party risk; exceptions reported to senior management / management body; give PRA related-party exposure details on request (based on CRD Art. 88(1)). Related party includes entities where a management-body member or close family holds ≥ 10% or has significant influence.
citation: PRA Rulebook, Related Party Transaction Risk Part (version 01/08/2025); CRD Art. 88 (legislation.gov.uk)

rule: No regulatory sector cap. Concentration is handled through Pillar 2A capital add-ons for single-name, sector and geographic concentration, measured with a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) on wholesale credit.
citation: PRA Statement of Policy "Pillar 2 methodologies", Ch. 6 Credit concentration risk (version 16/05/2024)

rule: No PRA numeric leverage cap or UK equivalent of the US guidance found. PRA named leveraged lending among higher-risk portfolios for credit risk management review (2025 priorities letter) and ran a thematic review of private-equity-related financing (2024 Dear CRO letter).
citation: PRA, UK deposit takers 2025 priorities letter (21 Jan 2025); PRA thematic review of PE-related financing (2024)

rule: Corporate obligor rating scale: at least 7 grades for non-defaulted obligors + 1 for defaulted. Rating assignments and reviews must be done or approved by an independent party that does not benefit from the credit decision. Ratings reviewed at least annually; higher-risk and problem exposures more often.
citation: PRA Rulebook, Credit Risk: IRB Approach (CRR) Part (effective 01/01/2027), Arts 170(1)(b), 173(1)(a)-(b)

rule: No single PRA rule found that prescribes a credit-policy template, approval authority matrix or annual corporate review for standardised-approach banks. Expectations sit in general systems-and-controls rules and supervisory letters.

UK banks use IFRS 9 expected credit loss (3 stages). No PRA numeric provision floor found. PRA's Sept 2026 thematic letter focuses on timely recognition of credit risk, staging, post-model adjustments and LGD/recovery assumptions; self-assessment ahead of a 2027 review.
citation: PRA letter, "Thematic feedback on accounting for IFRS 9 ECL", D. Bailey, 30 Sep 2026

rule: Basel 3.1 rules take effect 1 January 2027 (FRTB internal models: 1 January 2028). Final rules published in PS1/26 on 20 January 2026 (earlier near-final rules: PS17/23 and PS9/24).
Total RWA = max(un-floored RWA; 72.5% × standardised RWA + adjustment). Optional transition: 60% (2027), 65% (2028), 70% (2029); 72.5% applies thereafter (2030 inferred from text).
citation: PRA Rulebook, Required Level of Own Funds (CRR), Art. 92(2A), 92(5) (version 01/01/2027)

rule: Large corporates = annual revenue > GBP 440m (3-year average, highest consolidation level). For this sub-class: Foundation IRB, or standardised where permission granted; Advanced IRB not allowed. Corporate PD floor 0.05%. FIRB LGD for senior unsecured non-financial corporate: 40% (financial sector entities: 45%).

Unrated SME (non-retail) corporates: 85% risk weight. Unrated corporates: more risk-sensitive option of 65% for investment grade / 135% for non-investment grade (secondary source). Removal of SME and infrastructure support factors offset by "lending adjustments" in Pillar 2A.
citation: PRA PS1/26 page (85%, lending adjustments); 65%/135% from secondary source (see Part B, confidence M)

parameter: Legal lending limit, single borrower (national banks and federal savings associations)
rule: Total loans to one borrower ≤ 15% of capital and surplus, plus an extra 10% if the excess is fully secured by readily marketable collateral (market value ≥ 100% of the excess, perfected). State banks follow their own state law (not covered here).
citation: 12 CFR 32.3(a) (eCFR, up to date as of 11/09/2026)

parameter: Definition of capital for the lending limit
rule: "Capital and surplus" = Tier 1 + Tier 2 capital + any allowance not already in Tier 2. For community banks using the CBLR framework: Tier 1 + allowance.

Loans are combined when proceeds directly benefit another person, or a "common enterprise" exists (same repayment source with no other adequate source; or common control plus ≥ 50% of gross receipts or expenditures from each other). Loans to a corporate group are capped at 50% of capital and surplus in total.

Exempt from the limit: loans fully secured by US government obligations, loans to or guaranteed by federal agencies, loans backed by state general obligations (with counsel opinion), loans secured by segregated deposits, certain commercial paper and bankers' acceptances.

No general interbank exemption in Part 32. A sale of federal funds longer than 1 business day counts as a loan (overnight fed funds excluded). Separately, Reg F: interday credit exposure to a correspondent not shown to be adequately capitalized ≤ 25% of the bank's total capital.

parameter: Single-counterparty credit limit (largest bank holding companies only)
rule: Covered companies (G-SIB BHCs, Category II and III BHCs): aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty ≤ 25% of Tier 1 capital. G-SIB to "major counterparty": ≤ 15% of Tier 1. Interdependence / control test required when exposure > 5% of Tier 1 (control presumed at ≥ 25% of voting securities). 0%-risk-weight sovereigns are "exempt counterparties".

No general "10% of capital" large-exposure reporting rule for all US banks was found. The OCC examiner booklet defines a "concentration of credit" as obligations > 25% of Tier 1 capital + allowance for credit losses (an examination concept, not a cap).
citation: OCC Bulletin 2026-49 (30 Sep 2026), Comptroller's Handbook "Concentrations of Credit" v3.0

rule: Credit to executive officers, directors, principal shareholders and their related interests must be on substantially the same terms (rates, collateral) as for non-insiders, with no more than normal repayment risk.

Credit above the higher of USD 25,000 or 5% of unimpaired capital and surplus needs prior approval by a majority of the full board (the interested party abstains). Any credit that would take one insider above USD 500,000 needs prior approval.

parameter: Reg O: individual and aggregate insider limits
rule: Individual insider: same as the bank's lending limit (15% + 10%). Aggregate to all insiders: ≤ 100% of unimpaired capital and surplus (banks with deposits < USD 100m may go up to 200% by annual board resolution, if conditions are met).
Other credit to the bank's own executive officers ≤ the higher of 2.5% of unimpaired capital and surplus or USD 25,000, and never above USD 100,000.
Covered transactions with a single affiliate ≤ 10% of the bank's capital stock and surplus.

Not a limit. Supervisory screening criteria: construction, land and land development loans ≥ 100% of total risk-based capital; or total CRE ≥ 300% of total risk-based capital with ≥ 50% growth in the prior 36 months. Either one means heightened risk management is expected. The guidance "does not establish a CRE concentration limit". No rescission found as of Nov 2026.
citation: Interagency CRE Concentration Guidance, effective 12 Dec 2006 (Fed SR 07-1; OCC Bulletin 2006-46)

rule: OCC and FDIC withdrew the 2013 Interagency Guidance on Leveraged Lending and the 2014 FAQs on 5 Dec 2025 (OCC Bulletin 2025-44). Their banks now apply general safe-and-sound lending principles (eight principles-based standards, including a bank-specific definition of "leveraged loan"). The Federal Reserve did not join; SR 13-3 is still shown on the Fed site and is not marked superseded. The old guidance flagged total debt/EBITDA > 6x for extra scrutiny.
citation: Sullivan & Cromwell memo, 9 Dec 2025; Fed SR 13-3 page

parameter: Internal rating systems (advanced approaches banks only)
rule: Wholesale obligor rating system: at least 7 grades for non-defaulted obligors + 1 for defaulted. Each obligor rating reviewed when material information arrives and no less often than annually.

parameter: Credit policy, independent credit review (all banks)
rule: No numeric rule. Agencies expect an independent credit risk review system (2020 interagency credit risk review guidance) and sound underwriting under the safety-and-soundness standards.
citation: Secondary summary only (M); see Part D

rule: Allowance for credit losses under FASB ASC 326 (CECL: lifetime expected losses, no stages). The Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit Losses (revised April 2023) applies from each bank's ASC 326 adoption. No regulatory % floor.
citation: 88 FR (27 Apr 2023) revised ACL policy statement; OCC Bulletin 2023-11

rule: Current rules: standardised approach (12 CFR 217) for all banks; advanced approaches (IRB-type) for the largest firms. Basel III endgame re-proposal issued 19 Mar 2026: it rescinds the 2023 proposal, uses an "expanded risk-based approach" for Category I and II firms, and its comments closed 18 Jun 2026. No final rule found as of 13 Nov 2026.
citation: Fed Board open meeting 19 Mar 2026; KPMG US reg alert 2026

rule: No US output floor in force. Treatment under the 2026 re-proposal not confirmed.
